title: Absent Guidelines
content:
Guidelines for Absences:
Unexcused: There is one unexcused absence per semester.
● The first unexcused absence results in a warning and a $10 fine.
● The second unexcused absence results in one strike and a $35 fine.
● Any other unexcused absences result in immediate probationary status. Tardiness at a
chapter meeting will be counted towards an unexcused absence.
Excused: Two excused absences a semester. The specified member will be fined $15 on the
third excused absence. Any excused absence after that will follow this equation: Fine = 20 x
(excused absences - 3). To acquire an excused absence, a member must inform the Vice
President of Membership at least 24 hours in advance.
Ample notice is defined as at least 24 hours before the event. Non-frequent occurrence is no
more than one recreational activity absence per semester.
The Vice President of Membership will record all absences and tardiness after each chapter
meeting. Members are responsible for verifying the accuracy of their attendance records and
addressing any discrepancies within 24 hours of notification. Every Tardy and Absence will be
notified.
Guidelines for Tardies:
● Tardies apply to all members, regardless of activity status. A tardy is defined as arriving
at a mandatory event at least five minutes after the assigned time.
○ If a member is more than twenty minutes late to a mandatory event, they will
receive an unexcused absence.
● For every two tardies, a member will be issued one unexcused absence.
Guidelines for Fines:
If fines are not paid on time, they will increase by $5 daily. After 10 days, the specified member
will be put on probation.
-- 1 of 2 --
Examples of Absences
Excused Absences:
1. Family and Personal Emergencies
Examples: Death, illness, or significant events in the family.
Notification Requirement: As soon as possible.
2. Mandatory Academic or Professional Commitments
Examples: Exams, job interviews, or compulsory workshops.
Notification Requirement: 24 hours in advance.
3. Health-related Issues
Examples: Sickness, doctor’s appointments, or mental health days.
Notification Requirement: As soon as possible, with documentation if available.
4. Religious or Cultural Observances
Examples: Holidays, ceremonies, or cultural events.
Notification Requirement: 48 hours in advance.
5. Unforeseeable Urgent Situations
Examples: Pet emergencies, sudden travel needs, or accidents.
Notification Requirement: As soon as possible.
Unexcused Absences:
1. Recreational Activities
Examples: Concerts, sports events, or outings.
Note: May be excused with ample notice and non-frequent occurrence.
2. Social and Personal Engagements
Examples: Dates, parties, or non-urgent personal errands.
Note: Fraternity obligations should take priority.
3. Routine Non-Emergency Commitments
Examples: Regular gym sessions, casual meet-ups, or hobby classes.
Note: These should be scheduled around fraternity commitments.
4. Avoidable Absences
Examples: Oversleeping, lack of transport planning, Tardiness, or forgetfulness.
Note: These demonstrate a need for prioritization and planning.
-- 2 of 2 --

title: KTP Code of Conduct
content:
Kappa Theta Pi - Mu Chapter will not tolerate harassment in any form. Violation of the Policy subjects an
offending person to disciplinary action, including expulsion from the Fraternity. This policy applies to all
organizational members.
All organizational members are protected from harassment, including, but not limited to, harassment
according to their race, ethnicity, age, gender, gender identity, disability, sexual orientation, and religion.
Harassment is more than insensitivity or conduct that offends or creates an uncomfortable situation. Any
words or acts designed to disregard the safety or rights of another and which intimidate, degrade,
demean, threaten, and/or haze will not be tolerated on the basis of the standards of Kappa Theta Pi - Mu
Chapter. Such physical, psychological, verbal, electronic, and/or written acts directed toward an individual
or group of individuals are prohibited.
Harassment in any form is unacceptable because it is demeaning to another person and undermines the
integrity of the Fraternity. Organizational members should always treat others respectfully and with dignity
in a manner that does not offend another person's sensibilities.
Policy 1. Discrimination
Discrimination against or harassment of any individual for the reason of race, ethnicity, creed, religion,
sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, disability or veteran status is
specifically prohibited. Accordingly, equal access to employment opportunities, membership, educational
programs, financial assistance, and all other fraternal activities is extended to all persons.
Policy 2. Assault & Battery
In any activity or event sponsored or endorsed by Kappa Theta Pi - Mu Chapter, no chapter, member or
guest will engage in or permit assault and battery as defined in the state statutes in which the activity or
event occurs.
Physical Violence: Physical violence or threats thereof will not be tolerated under any circumstances.
Policy 3. Sexual Misconduct
No organizational member or guest will engage in or permit sexist or sexually abusive behavior, sexual
harassment, non-consensual sexual activity, sexual violence, domestic violence, dating violence, stalking,
or sexual exploitation. For the purposes of this policy:
● Consent is the affirmative, unambiguous, and voluntary agreement to engage in a specific sexual
activity during a sexual encounter.
● Sexual harassment is unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature.
● Sexual violence is any physical or sexual act perpetrated against a person’s will or where a
person is incapable of giving consent (e.g., due to an individual’s age or use of drugs or alcohol,
or because of an intellectual or other disability prevents the individual from having the capacity to
give consent).
● Domestic violence is an abusive behavior used by an intimate partner to gain or maintain power
and control over the other intimate partner. Domestic violence can be physical, sexual, emotional,
economic, or psychological actions or threats of actions that influence another person.
● Dating violence is defined as violence committed by a person who is or has been in a social
relationship of a romantic or intimate nature with the victim; and where the existence of such a
relationship will be determined based on a consideration of the following factors: the length of the
-- 1 of 6 --
relationship, the type of relationship, and the frequency of interaction between the persons
involved in the relationship.
● Stalking is defined as a pattern of repeated and unwanted attention, harassment, contact, or any
other course of conduct directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to
feel fear.
● Sexual exploitation occurs when a person takes non-consensual or abusive sexual advantage of
another for his/her own advantage or benefit, or to benefit or advantage anyone other than the
one being exploited. That behavior does not otherwise constitute one of other sexual misconduct
offenses.
Policy 4. Sexual Harassment
Harassment and Bullying: Harassment or any form of intimidation is unacceptable. However, it's
recognized that sometimes jokes among friends can be misconstrued. In such cases, intent and context
will be considered, and the matter may be subject to review.
Kappa Theta Pi - Mu Chapter will not tolerate sexual harassment in any form. Violation of this policy
subjects an offending person to disciplinary action, including expulsion from the Fraternity. This policy
applies to all Fraternity collegiate members, pledges, alumni members, officers, directors, and employees.
[\]
Definition: Sexual harassment consists of unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favors or
other verbal or physical acts of a sexual nature where:
- Submission to such conduct is made either explicitly or implicitly a term or condition of
membership in the Fraternity or
- A Fraternity decision is based on an individual's acceptance or rejection of such conduct or
- Such conduct interferes with an individual's membership in the Fraternity or work for the
Fraternity or creates an environment that is intimidating, hostile, or offensive to a reasonable
person of the same sex as the recipient.
Sexual harassment is a form of misconduct that is unacceptable because it is demeaning to another
person and undermines the integrity of the Fraternity. Fraternity members and pledges at all times should
treat others respectfully and with dignity in a manner that does not offend another person's sensibilities.
Actions taken by nonmembers relating to Fraternity business may also constitute sexual harassment and
should be promptly reported.
A violation may include, but is not limited to:
● Any action or statement of a sexual nature which is embarrassing, harassing, intimidating, or
abusive;
● Unwanted comments, communications, jokes, or requests of a sexual nature;
● Unwelcome and persistent sexually explicit statements or stories;
● Repeated use of sexually degrading words, gestures, or sounds to describe a person;
● Recurring derogatory comments or questions about an individual's sexual orientation and/or
behavior;
● Any kind of unwelcome sexual advances;
● Repeated phone calls, messages, and/or other communications sexual in nature, even after
statements have there is no interest;
-- 2 of 6 --
● Threats of retaliation as a result of a sexual encounter;
● Implied or stated threats of sexual violence;
● Sexual harassment can occur with any gender, gender identities/expressions, and/or sexual
orientation.
Policy 8. Alcohol
Responsibility: If alcohol is consumed at fraternity events, it should be done responsibly and within legal
limits.
Policy 9. Attendance
Mandatory Meetings: Members are expected to attend all mandatory meetings. If a member cannot
attend due to an unavoidable conflict, they should email kappathetapiutd@gmail.com at least 24 hours
in advance.
Event Participation: Active participation in fraternity events is mandatory. A consistent lack of
participation without a valid reason will be subject to review.
Committee Commitment: Members who are a part of specific committees have a responsibility not only
to the broader fraternity but also to their respective committees. Consistent participation and active
involvement in committee events, tasks, and initiatives are essential.
Committee Meetings: Committee members should prioritize attendance at all scheduled committee
meetings. These sessions play a pivotal role in the planning, coordination, and execution of committee
tasks, and every member's input is invaluable.
Notification of Absence: If a committee member cannot attend a scheduled meeting due to unforeseen
circumstances, it's essential to notify the committee chair or the relevant point of contact as soon as
possible, preferably 24 hours in advance.
Value Contribution: It's not just about attendance; it's about contributing value. Members should come
prepared to meetings, actively engage in discussions, and collaborate effectively with peers to ensure
meeting the committee's objectives.
Review of Participation: A member's consistent absence or lack of active participation in committee
meetings and events without a genuine reason may lead to a review by the committee chair and, if
necessary, the fraternity leadership.
Policy 5. Open Dating Policy
Kappa Theta Pi - Mu Chapter is committed to fostering an environment where all members, regardless of
gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, or relationship status, are treated with respect, dignity, and
fairness. We emphasize the importance of clear communication, consent, and the availability of resources
for support. This policy applied to all fraternity members, pledges, alumni, and officers.
Definition: Open dating involves engaging in romantic or intimate relationships within the fraternity while
adhering to consent, respect, and open communication principles.
Guidelines and Expectations:
1. Consent: All members engaging in romantic or intimate relationships within the fraternity
must ensure that consent is affirmative, unambiguous, and voluntary. Consent should be
given explicitly for each sexual activity during a sexual encounter.
-- 3 of 6 --
2. Respectful Communication: Members engaging in relationships must communicate
openly, honestly, and respectfully with their partners. They should discuss boundaries,
expectations, and concerns to ensure a healthy and consensual relationship.
3. Confidentiality and Compliance Reporting: Any member who experiences discomfort,
harassment, or any form of misconduct within a relationship is encouraged to report the
incident to the designated compliance head or any authority you feel comfortable with
within the fraternity. All reports will be handled confidentially, and appropriate actions will
be taken to address the issue.
4. No Retaliation: Retaliation against any member who reports an incident, raises concern,
or seeks assistance regarding a relationship issue is strictly prohibited. The fraternity is
committed to protecting the rights and well-being of those who come forward.
5. Enforcement and Accountability: Violation of this policy may result in disciplinary
action, which includes warning, education, suspension, or expulsion from the fraternity,
depending on the severity and recurrence of the violation.
Policy 6. Interaction with Pledges
Kappa Theta Pi - Mu Chapter recognizes the importance of fostering a positive, respectful environment
for all members, including pledges. The policy provides guidelines on how organizational members should
conduct themselves when interacting with pledges, ensuring a supportive and educational experience
during the pledge process.
Guidelines and Expectations:
1. Respectful Treatment: All organizational members must treat pledges with respect,
fairness, and professionalism. Hazing, discrimination, harassment, or intimidation
towards pledges is strictly prohibited.
2. Guidance and Mentorship: Organizational members should offer guidance, mentorship,
and support to pledges throughout the pledging process. Encourage their personal and
professional growth while upholding the values and mission of Kappa Theta Pi - Mu
Chapter.
3. Education on Fraternity Values: Pledges should be educated about the fraternity’s
values, goals, and expectations. Members are encouraged to help pledges understand
and align with the principles and standards of the fraternity.
4. No Discrimination: Pledges should not be subjected to discrimination based on race,
ethnicity, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national
origin, age, or disability.
5. Maintaining Professionalism: All interactions with pledges should be conducted
professionally and appropriately, Any person or romantic relationship with a pledge is
strictly prohibited during the pledging period.
Policy 7. Relationships with Pledges
Kappa Theta Pi - Mu Chapter emphasized the importance of maintaining appropriate boundaries and
fostering a healthy, professional environment during pledging. This policy outlines the fraternity’s stance
on relationships with pledges.
Guidelines and Expectations:
-- 4 of 6 --
1. No Romantic Relations During Pledging: Organizational members are not allowed to
initiate or engage in romantic relationships with pledges while in the pledging process.
This includes any form of dating, romantic involvement, or intimate relationships.
2. Prior Relationships: If an organization member is already in a romantic relationship with
an individual who subsequently becomes a pledge, the fraternity understands and
respects this relationship. However, both parties should act professionally and maintain
appropriate boundaries during pledging.
3. Transparency and Accountability: If a pre-existing relationship exists between an
organizational member and a pledge, both parties should promptly inform the appropriate
fraternity authorities to ensure transparency and adherence to fraternity policies.
4. Post-Pledging Relationships: Once the pledging period is successfully completed, and
the pledge becomes a full member of the fraternity, any existing relationship can continue
without restriction, provided it aligns with the values and policies of Kappa Theta Pi - Mu
Chapter.
2. Representation and Public Behavior:
Respectful Representation: Members should always represent the fraternity positively and respectfully,
both in person and online.
Public Criticism: Openly criticizing or denigrating the fraternity or its members in public forums, including
social media, is strictly prohibited.
Confidentiality: Internal matters, discussions, or confidential information should not be shared outside of
the fraternity.
5. Financial Responsibility:
Dues: Members are expected to pay their dues on time. If a member faces financial difficulties, they
should approach the current executive board to discuss potential solutions.
Fraternity Property: Members should respect and take care of any property belonging to the fraternity.
6. General Behavior:
Leadership Respect: Members should respect the decisions and directives of fraternity leadership while
feeling empowered to voice their opinions in appropriate forums.
Every member of Kappa Theta Pi should strive to uphold these standards, not just for the reputation of
our fraternity but also for personal growth and the betterment of our community. Violations of this Code of
Conduct may be subject to review and potential disciplinary action.
Kappa Theta Pi - Mu Chapter is deeply committed to ensuring that every member, particularly the
pledges, experiences a nurturing, respectful, and enriching environment that aligns with our fraternity
values and ethos. This policy outlines the standards of behavior expected when interacting with pledges.
Guidelines and Expectations:
Positive Reinforcement: Encourage pledges through positive reinforcement rather than criticism.
Recognize their efforts and contributions to foster a sense of belonging and motivation.
Clear Boundaries: Maintain clear and professional boundaries. Personal and romantic relationships
between organizational members and pledges are strictly prohibited during the pledging period to avoid
conflicts of interest or perceived favoritism.
-- 5 of 6 --
Open Communication: Maintain transparent lines of communication. Pledges should feel comfortable
seeking guidance, asking questions, or voicing concerns without fear of retribution.
Nurturing Environment: Avoid intimidating actions, words, or behaviors. Instead, create an environment
where pledges can thrive, learn, and grow.
Zero Tolerance for Hazing: Hazing in any form is strictly prohibited. Any member engaging in or
promoting hazing activities will face immediate disciplinary action.
Role Modeling: As seasoned fraternity members, your actions, words, and behaviors are models for the
pledges. Uphold the highest standards of conduct and integrity and exemplify what it means to be a part
of Kappa Theta Pi - Mu Chapter.
Constructive Feedback: If feedback is required, ensure it is constructive, respectful, and provided in a
manner that aids the pledge's development rather than diminishes their confidence.
-- 6 of 6 --

title: KTP Strike System Framework
content:
Strike System Framework:
Infractions & Penalties:
The following is how a brother can acquire a strike:
● Missing a meeting without prior notice.
● Repeated Absences.
● Repeated tardiness.
● Neglecting fraternity duties.
● Negative comments about the fraternity.
● Inappropriate actions or statements.
● Not paying fines on time.
Tiered disciplinary System
The fraternity's disciplinary system is structured in tiers, with each level of consequence building
upon the last. Strikes are the highest degree of consequence, followed by fines and point
deductions.
● Strikes: The most severe consequence, reserved for serious and/or repeated
infractions. All strikes are accompanied by a fine and a point deduction.
● Fines: A monetary penalty for specific infractions. All fines are accompanied by a point
deduction.
● Point Deductions: The lowest level of consequence. Point deductions can be issued
alone for minor infractions or as a component of a strike or fine.
Strikes outline:
1 Strike: A formal written warning, a point deduction, and a fine. The fine will be determined by
the specific infraction that resulted in the strike, as outlined in the fraternity's constitution and
bylaws. For instance, an unexcused absence that results in a strike will carry the associated fine
from the constitution.
2 Strikes: Brothers/Pledges who accumulate two strikes will be required to meet with the
Internal Affairs Committee for a thorough review of their behavior. Additionally, they will receive
another fine and a point deduction. During this process, the leadership will determine
appropriate remediation tasks tailored to the individual’s situation. The committee will evaluate
the individual's alignment with fraternity values and commitment, considering the nature and
severity of the infractions. Continued membership will be contingent upon successful completion
of assigned remediation and a demonstrated willingness to grow and improve.
3 Strikes: Immediate removal from the fraternity. The decision will be final, and the individual’s
membership will be terminated with no opportunity for remediation.
-- 1 of 2 --
Individuals who accumulate two strikes will be temporarily inactive for a duration determined
by the leadership, considering the nature and severity of the infractions. During this period, the
member may be required to complete remediation tasks determined by leadership. The
leadership will also reassess the individual's membership in the Kappa Theta Pi - Mu
Chapter, questioning their alignment with fraternity values and commitment. The decision
regarding continued membership will be made after a thorough evaluation, considering the
member’s past contributions, the nature of their infractions, the results of the remediation tasks,
and their potential for growth and change.
Duration: Strikes have a shelf life of one academic semester. At the start of each new
semester, all members will begin with a clean slate.
Right to Appeal: All Active Members have the right to dispute a strike if they believe it was
issued in error or is unjustified. Appeals must be submitted to the Internal Affairs Committee for
review.
Removal of Strikes: Members may reduce active strikes by demonstrating consistent positive
behavior, active engagement, and contribution to fraternity events. For example, if a member
has two strikes during the current semester, they may have one removed by the end of the
semester based on commendable conduct, as determined by the Executive Board

content:
KAPPA THETA PI CONSTITUTION
Date: 03/01/2026
PREAMBLE
We, the active members of Kappa Theta Pi Professional Fraternity at the
University of Texas at Dallas establishes this Constitution to execute our purpose,
functions, and progression.
Table of Contents

-- 3 of 32 --
ARTICLE I: Organization
Section 1: Name
The name of this fraternity shall be “Kappa Theta Pi, Professional Technology
Fraternity,” henceforth referred to as “Kappa Theta Pi” or “KTP.”
Section 2: Letters
The letters of this fraternity shall be ΚΘΠ, which signifies a “Love for Technology.”
Section 3: Advisor
Our advisor is Srimathi Srinivasan, a professor at UTD.
Section 4: Funds
Funds will be derived from membership dues, fundraisers, etc. The Executive
Board will manage funds and approve all expenses.
-- 4 of 32 --
ARTICLE II: Statement of Purpose
1. Build an active community of students with a shared interest in technology.
2. Sponsor events and activities promoting intellectual, technical, professional,
and social development.
3. Provide career guidance to members.
4. Foster relationships among members, students, alumni, faculty members,
the local community, and businesses.
5. Provide service and philanthropy to the local community.
6. Maintain lifelong cooperation and friendship among the members of this
fraternity.
7. Kappa Theta Pi is committed to a policy of equal opportunity for all persons
and does not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, age, marital
status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, disability,
religion, height, weight, or veteran status in its membership or activities
unless permitted by university policy for gender-specific organizations.
-- 5 of 32 --
ARTICLE III: Membership
Section 1: Terminology
1. The Pledging process is the first semester of membership within the
fraternity.
2. A Pledge is a member undergoing the Pledging process.
3. The Rush is the process by which the fraternity is introduced to Pledge
candidates and decides which candidates shall proceed into the Pledging
process. A Pledge candidate undergoing the Rushing process may be called
a Rushee.
4. An Active is a fraternity member who has successfully exited the Pledging
process, is a current student at the University of Texas at Dallas (the
University), and is in otherwise good standing (see Article III) with the
fraternity.
5. An Inactive is a fraternity member who is not currently participating in
fraternity requirements but will return to active status at the end of the
semester.
6. An Alumnus is a former active student who has graduated from the
university and was in good standing with the fraternity in their last semester
of enrollment.
7. In our fraternity hierarchy, Executive Members hold the highest authority
and are responsible for leadership, decision-making, and guiding the
fraternity’s direction. Active Members come next, participating fully in
-- 6 of 32 --
events and supporting executive decisions. Inactive Members follow as
those who, though temporarily not participating, retain their membership
status and may re-engage. Alumni are valued for their past contributions
and offer mentorship, while Pledges are at the introductory level, learning
about the fraternity and aspiring to join the active membership by
demonstrating commitment and respect for our values.
8. It is crucial for pledges to respect the positions of each brother, as this
respect reflects their dedication to the fraternity’s values and commitment
to becoming part of the brotherhood. Failure to show proper regard for
each role disrupts the unity and order that define our fraternity. Any
disrespect towards a brother can lead to disciplinary action, as honoring
these roles is a fundamental expectation for pledges aspiring to join as full
members.
Section 2: Eligibility
A Rushee who wishes to enter the Pledging process must reasonably expect to
remain at the University for at least one more semester, excluding their Pledging
semester.
Section 3: Rush
1. At the beginning of the fall and spring semesters, the Vice President of
Membership and Director of Rush will arrange advertising, informational
sessions, events, and applications for potential members with assistance
from involved members.
2. Rush shall begin with informational sessions that provide an overview of
the fraternity to interested students.
-- 7 of 32 --
3. After attending an informational session, all students interested in
becoming members of Kappa Theta Pi must fill out an application to acquire
clerical information and a summary of their interests.
4. Events are for students interested in becoming active members. The Vice
President of Membership and involved members will organize the rush
events. At each event, attendance, participation, and overall behavior will
be factors that determine eligibility for a bid.
5. After the Rush process, the executive board will hold a technical and
behavioral interview. At least three Executive Board members will be
present at each interview.
6. A selection meeting will be called within 7 days of the last interview,
comprising all eligible active members to determine the Pledge class. Active
members must attend two Rush events to vote at the selection meeting. All
available members of the fraternity conduct the selection meeting, and the
Vice President of Membership or Director of Rush will present the pledges.
Via discussions and voting, bids are assigned to potential members based
on talent and fraternity needs. The Executive Board holds the final decision
for all bids.
Section 4: Pledging
1. As Pledges of Kappa Theta Pi, they shall be required to participate in the
events and onboarding requirements decided by the Vice President of
Membership to create bonds amongst other pledges and active members
and foster commitment to KTP. Failure to complete all of the requirements,
-- 8 of 32 --
unless overridden by a 2/3 majority decision of the Executive Board, shall
result in loss of a Bid.
2. Big and Little pairings shall be decided within 7 weeks after pledge
initiation. If interested, an active member shall be paired with one Pledge.
The Vice President of Membership shall determine secret gift offerings,
informal interviews, or other requirements. If the number of pledges
exceeds the number of active members wanting a little, the actives can
choose to take more than one little. If there are more pledges than active
members willing to take a Little, the Executive Board will determine
alternative pairings or mentorship arrangements.
3. Pledges are expected to interact with all active and executive members with
the utmost respect and professionalism. Any behavior that undermines the
dignity of the fraternity, its members, or its leadership will be subject to
disciplinary action.
4. Pledges shall be subject to a distinct disciplinary system, separate from the
3-Strike System governing active members. This pledge-specific system, as
defined in the 'Pledge Code of Conduct,' is based on tracking infractions,
and pledges do not accrue strikes as defined in Article IV, Section 9.
Disciplinary actions are determined by the Executive Board and may include
fines, additional requirements, or termination of the pledge process. (KTP
Code of Conduct and Absent Guidelines).
5. Until a Pledge becomes an Active, they shall be conducted under a strict
'Dry' policy for the entirety of the pledge program. This Dry Pledge Rules
prohibits any and all association with alcohol and controlled substances.
-- 9 of 32 --
a. Prohibited activities include, but are not limited to:
i. The consumption, possession, holding, or distribution of such
substances.
ii. Knowingly being in the immediate vicinity where such
substances are being consumed. * Appearing in person or in
social media content (such as posts or photos) where such
substances are present.
b. Pledges are also prohibited from appearing to be under the influence
of alcohol or controlled substances in public or on social media.
Additionally, pledges may not post, share, or engage with any content
involving alcohol or substance use on social media platforms for the
duration of the program.
c. Any violation of this policy [dry pledging] will result in immediate
disciplinary action, which will include a formal infraction. Leading to
an immediate meeting with the Executive Board and being exited
from the fraternity.
i. Any brother found hiding, protecting, or enabling a pledge to
violate the Dry Pledging Process, including but not limited to,
the use, possession, or appearance of alcohol or controlled
substances, will be held equally accountable and subject to the
same disciplinary consequences deemed by the Vice President
of Internal Affairs .
-- 10 of 32 --
6. At a Crossover event at the end of each semester, pledges who complete
the pledging process shall become active members.
7. The pledging process is a probationary trial period intended to assess a
pledge’s character, trustworthiness, and commitment to the fraternity’s
values and mission. As pledges are candidates for membership, they are not
afforded the rights or privileges of active members as defined in this
Constitution.
8. The Executive Board reserves the right to revoke a pledge's bid and
terminate their pledging process at any point, with or without cause, by a
2/3 majority decision. This authority is separate from and in addition to the
loss of a bid resulting from failure to complete specified requirements.
Section 5: Active Membership
Active members must meet all requirements stated in Article IV.
Section 6: Alumni
1. An Alumni Member shall be defined as an individual who has been duly
initiated into active membership of Kappa Theta Pi and has subsequently
graduated from the University of Texas at Dallas.
2. Alumni status is granted after graduation but may be held if the individual
wishes to remain active as a master’s student.
3. At a Crossover event at the end of each semester, each graduating active
member, not on probation, shall become an honored alumni member.
4. Alumni members may attend future fraternity events, provided there is
sufficient space and available funding to accommodate them.
-- 11 of 32 --
5. An annual newsletter shall be sent to alumni members, highlighting the
year’s achievements and direction for the future.
6. Prior to the Crossover event, all alumni must transfer their roles and
responsibilities to a successor they trust or to an individual approved by the
Executive Board.
7. All alumni must cease active duties immediately following the Crossover
event.
8. Alumni shall not participate in any fraternity activities or operations unless
explicitly approved by the Executive Board.
9. Alumni shall not interfere with the internal affairs, decision-making
processes, or operations of the fraternity unless given express permission
by the Executive Board.
ARTICLE IV: Membership Requirements
1. Membership shall be open to students of The University of Texas at Dallas
regardless of sex (unless specifically exempt by law), race, color, religion,
age, national origin, disability, or veteran status.
2. Membership must be limited to UT Dallas students, faculty, and staff.
Section 1: Assessments
1. Active brothers must maintain a minimum cumulative grade point average
of 3.0.
-- 12 of 32 --
2. Active members shall be able to name and identify the current Executive
Board.
3. Active members shall not be a member of any other professional fraternity.
Section 2: Dues
1. Each semester, the Executive Board shall determine dues, and the funds
collected shall be used to reserve rooms for chapter meetings, fund social
events, pay fees, or any other expenditure for the fraternity.
2. If there is reason to believe that funds are not being used for the benefit of
KTP, members in charge of the finances will have an academic hearing and
be voted on by all members about the future of KTP.
3. The Vice President of Finance shall collect the payments, or a different
member of the Executive Board voted for this role and deposit them into
the fraternity’s official bank account.
4. The Executive Board may assess any additional fees at any time.
5. If members cannot afford dues, they must contact the Executive Board in
writing to determine an alternative plan that the Executive Board sees fit.
Section 3: Attendance
1. Attendance at all chapter meetings and any event the Executive Board
determines is mandatory shall be logged.
2. Members must notify the Vice President of Membership at least 24 hours in
advance to receive an excused absence via the official KTP email.
-- 13 of 32 --
3. Excused Absences: Members are allowed two excused absences per
semester.
a. The specified member will be fined $15 on the third excused
absence.
b. Any excused absence after that will follow this equation: Fine = 20 x
(excused absences - 3).
c. The Vice President of Membership will record all absences and
tardiness after each chapter meeting. Members are responsible for
verifying the accuracy of their attendance records and addressing any
discrepancies within 24 hours of notification. Every Tardy and
Absence will be notified.
4. Unexcused Absences
a. Failure to receive an excused absence will be recorded as an
unexcused absence.
b. There are two unexcused absences per semester.
i. The first unexcused absence will result in a warning and a $10
fine.
ii. The second unexcused absence is a strike and a $35 fine. Any
other unexcused absences result in immediate probationary
status. Tardiness at a chapter meeting will be counted towards
an unexcused absence.
5. Tardies
-- 14 of 32 --
a. Tardiness applies to all members and is defined as arriving five
minutes after the assigned event time.
b. For every two tardies, a member will receive one unexcused absence.
c. If a member is more than twenty minutes late, they will receive an
unexcused absence.
Section 4: Professional Development
1. All active members shall be expected to participate in two professional
development events per semester organized by the Vice President of
Professional Development.
Section 5: Committees and Individual Tasks
1. Vice Presidents may choose to maintain a committee throughout the
semester.
a. If so, the committees will have meetings and aid the Vice President.
2. Vice Presidents who choose not to maintain a committee will be
responsible for actively requesting help to accomplish tasks.
a. Members should inform Vice Presidents that they are working on a
task.
3. Committees may be added and dropped based on the needs of the
fraternity.
Section 6: Inactive
-- 15 of 32 --
1. Each member with active standing in the fraternity for one semester or
more is entitled to one semester of Inactive Status for study abroad,
internship, or personal reasons.
a. A member may only be inactive for more than one semester under
special circumstances, which will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis
by The Executive Board. An example of an approved exception would
be an extended study abroad program lasting more than one
semester.
2. To acquire Inactive Status, the requesting member must fill out the Inactive
Status application form, located in the drive or available on request from
The Executive Board. The Executive Board shall determine whether or not
to grant the status.
3. Inactive Status requests are due by the end of the pledge bid process.
Section 7: Status Change
1. All activity statuses shall be finalized by the time bids are issued. Any
member seeking to change their activity status must initiate the process by
contacting the Vice President of Membership.
2. Members are not allowed to go inactive the semester before the semester
of their graduation. In addition members are also not allowed to go inactive
the semester of their graduation. Either members must stay active or must
formally drop from the fraternity. Exceptions can be made in certain
circumstances with proper documentation.
-- 16 of 32 --
3. Once bids have been issued, the activity status of any member shall remain
unchanged, except where the Executive Board, at its sole discretion,
determines that a change is warranted.
4. If a member needs to temporarily step back from active participation due to
a family emergency or other personal reasons, the member should reach
out to the executive team to request a change in their status from active to
inactive. This change is subject to the approval of the executive team, and
supporting documentation may be required.
5. Similarly, if a member wishes to return to active status from inactive, they
should also contact the executive team for approval.
Section 8: Probation
1. Probation is when a member is forcibly put on inactive status and is not
allowed participation of any capacity with the fraternity.
2. A member can be put on probation at any period of time as deemed
appropriate by the Executive Board. The probationary period is also
dependent on the remediation tasks or the severity of the case.
3. An exit interview shall be a meeting between a member on probation and
at least two Executive Board members. The exit interview is a formal way to
give members an honorable way to drop out. The Executive Board can
initiate the exit interview process with members whenever they feel
appropriate.
4. A member on probation shall be unable to vote or attend any social
gatherings unless the social event is taking place at the current residence of
the probated member.
-- 17 of 32 --
5. Members on probation are not eligible to run for any leadership positions
Section 9: Disciplinary Strike System
1. All Strikes will be specified in the KTP Strike System Framework.
2. Kappa Theta Pi will operate under a 3-Strike System:
a. Strike 1: Formal warning and a $20 fine.
b. Strike 2: Mandatory meeting with the Internal Affairs Committee to
evaluate continued membership in Kappa Theta Pi.
c. Strike 3: Immediate removal from the fraternity.
3. All Active Members have the right to dispute a strike if they believe it was
issued in error or is unjustified.
ARTICLE V: Bylaws
Section 1: Governance
The laws governing Kappa Theta Pi are in this Constitution.
Section 2: Chapter Meetings
A weekly chapter meeting shall be held to discuss the current events and status of
the fraternity. Unless otherwise instructed, all active members and pledges must
attend all chapter meetings. In order to be granted absence from a meeting,

24 hours in advance.
Section 3: Social Gatherings
A social gathering for members of this fraternity shall be held at least three times
per semester. Funds from the fraternity's account shall be used to host these
events.
Section 4: Professional Development
At least three professional development events shall occur per semester. These
events may include, but are not limited to, resume-building workshops,
professional photo shoots, internship panels, career counseling, and corporate
visits.
Section 5: Voting
For all voting cases, a majority vote of 2/3 of a quorum is necessary to pass the
motion, such as Executive Board elections and amendments to the Constitution.

Section 1: Purpose
The function of the Executive Board is to manage the fraternity and best serve its
members.
Section 2: Management
1. The Executive Board shall schedule chapter meetings and events.

Section 3: Post-Election Transition Period
1. Following the conclusion of elections, the newly elected Executive Board
members shall serve as officers-elect in a transitional training role. They will

2. Outgoing Executive Board members are required to provide shadowing
opportunities and mentorship to their successors. This period shall include

Section 5: Elections
1. An eligible voter in an Executive Board election must maintain Active status
on the election date.
2. An eligible candidate for Vice President of Finance, Vice President of
Communication, Vice President of Technology, Vice President of
Engagement, Vice President of Professional Development, or Vice President
of Membership must maintain Active status on the election date.
a. If, for some circumstances, the majority of current active members
cannot run for an executive position, newly crossed-over pledges can
run for an executive position.
3. An eligible candidate for President must maintain Active status on the
election date and must have served on the executive board previously, in
addition maintained Active status for at least two full semesters.
4. A member with a probation record is not an eligible candidate for any
Executive Board position.
-- 26 of 32 --
5. An eligible voter who cannot attend the election may cast their vote by
presenting a signed absentee ballot to the Executive Board before the start
of the election.
6. A majority vote of 2/3 of a quorum shall be necessary to attain an office. If a
majority is not reached, the candidate receiving the lowest number of votes
cast is dropped from the ballot, and a re-vote is taken of the remaining
candidates until a majority is received.
7. A petition of 1/3 of the total active members shall be necessary to raise the
question of removing an officer or a member before the next chapter
meeting. A 2/3 majority vote is required to remove an officer from their
office. A 2/3 majority vote is needed to remove a member from the
fraternity. This process is reserved for unforeseen or egregious
circumstances that warrant immediate removal, and it operates separately
from the three-strike disciplinary system. After reading the charges, the
impeachment issue shall be discussed and voted upon at the meeting.
8. An Executive Board appointment shall take place on an as-needed basis.
The option for voting will be available, but appointment will be the first
course of action.
9. The sitting Executive Board officers are responsible for transitioning their
responsibilities throughout the semester in which the election takes place.
The newly elected Executive Board officers shall take on their full
responsibilities at the end of the semester in which they are voted in.
10.If KTP is dissolved, the remaining funds will be allocated to any current
projects that KTP’s brothers will carry on.
Section 6: Accountability
-- 27 of 32 --
All Executive Board actions and positions are subject to review and revision
provided a 2/3 majority active member quorum is in disagreement.
Section 7: Final Authority of the Executive Board
The Executive Board shall hold the ultimate authority in all matters concerning the
governance, operations, and decision-making of Kappa Theta Pi. All decisions
made by the Executive Board shall be deemed final and binding, subject to the
provisions of this Constitution. Any decision made by the Executive Board may be
appealed by a petition signed by at least 25% of active members, prompting a
vote by the full membership. The Executive Board reserves the right to review,
amend, or overrule decisions made by any committee, subcommittee, or
individual member of the organization.
Section 8: Director Appointments and Removal
The Executive Board shall have the authority to appoint and remove directors at
any point in the semester to address the evolving needs of the fraternity. The
appointment of a director shall require a majority vote of the Executive Board. The
removal of a director shall require a 2/3 majority vote of the Executive Board.
